exposure: Baseline body mass index (BMI) categorized as normoweight (18.5-24.9 kg/m2), overweight (25-29.9 kg/m2), or obese (≥ 30 kg/m2)
outcome: Maternal-fetal complications during pregnancy, labor, and early puerperium
cohort: 1236 pregnant women who received care between January 2017 and May 2018
finding: While obese women had higher rates of prenatal complications, obesity and overweight were not associated with worse puerperium outcomes in this cohort.
mod_finding: The study found that maternal age and previous cesarean section, but not BMI, were risk factors for cesarean delivery.
